title: 'Quiet Questing' — Americans Want Switched Off Travel
paragraphs: For many people, a vacation is not always relaxing. They may have to plan everything, solve problems and make sure everyone else is happy. Now, according to a new survey, many Americans want a different kind of trip, where they can switch off and enjoy some peace and quiet.

The survey was carried out online by Talker Research in September 2026 for the hotel company IHG Hotels & Resorts. It asked 2,000 Americans who plan to travel in the next 12 months about their travel plans for 2027.

The most popular trend was "quiet questing," which was chosen by 31% of people. These are trips that focus on peace and getting away from phone notifications, crowds and responsibilities. They can include trips without phones, activities that do not use technology and silent retreats. The second most popular trend was experiencing places "like a local," at 29%.

The survey also found that many people feel tired after their trips. In fact, 51% said they always or often come home from a vacation completely exhausted. In addition, 67% said they see themselves as "hosts" in their daily lives, which means they make the plans and make sure everyone has a good time. The same number said that being in charge on a trip feels more like a job than a vacation.
When people were asked what they most wanted to leave behind on vacation, the top answers were cleaning, at 30%, cooking, at 28%, and making sure everyone else is happy, at 27%.
Gemma Bull of IHG said that travelers want trips that let them "step out of host mode and into vacation mode."
Interestingly, quiet questing was the top choice for every generation except Gen Z. Young people were more interested in living like a local.
